subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Natural raised banks of sediment along the edges of a river channel are called:
questions.explain: Levees are raised banks built up by repeated deposition during floods.

questions.q: Beach nourishment is an example of:
questions.explain: Beach nourishment, adding sand or shingle, is a soft engineering approach.

questions.q: Transport in which small particles bounce along the river bed is called:
questions.explain: Saltation is the bouncing or hopping of small particles along the bed.

questions.q: Which of these is HARD engineering coastal defence?
questions.explain: A sea wall is a hard engineering structure that reflects wave energy.

questions.q: On a coast with alternating hard and soft rock, resistant rock tends to form ____ and softer rock forms ____.
questions.explain: Resistant rock juts out as headlands while softer rock is eroded back into bays.

questions.q: The boundary separating one drainage basin from another is the:
questions.explain: The watershed is the ridge of high land marking the edge of a drainage basin.

questions.q: A flood hydrograph with a short lag time and high peak discharge usually indicates:
options: A gentle slow response, e.g. forested basin
A rapid flashy response, e.g. urban or impermeable basin
questions.explain: A short lag time and high peak show water reaching the river quickly, raising flood risk.

questions.q: A long ridge of sand or shingle joined to the land at one end and projecting into the sea is a:
questions.explain: A spit is a depositional ridge attached to the coast at one end, formed by longshore drift.

questions.q: When rocks knock together and become smaller and rounder, the process is:
questions.explain: Attrition wears rocks down as they collide, making them smaller and rounder.

questions.q: When a spit grows across a bay, joining two headlands and trapping a lagoon behind it, it forms a:
questions.explain: A bar forms where a spit extends across a bay, often enclosing a lagoon.

questions.q: Longshore drift is the process that:
options: Transports sediment ALONG the coast in a zig-zag motion
questions.explain: Longshore drift moves sediment along the coast as swash arrives at an angle and backwash returns straight down.

questions.q: Erosion caused by the sheer force of fast-moving water hitting and pushing into cracks in the bank is called:
questions.explain: Hydraulic action is the force of water compressing air in cracks, weakening rock.
